 Judgment

The injured claimant has preferred this appeal against the compensation awarded in M.C.O.P.No.54 of 2012 dated 30.11.2011 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Vellore (I Additional District and Sessions Court) on the ground of exoneration the 5th respondent/Insurance company.

1 2. For the sake of convenience the parties are referred as per ranking before the tribunal.

3. The factum of the accident, the manner of the accident and rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, are not disputed and hence, the finding rendered by the Tribunal is hereby confirmed.
4. On the point of liability of R5 all are heard.
5. The claimant was travelling in the motorcycle which has met with an accident on being hit by the tractor from trailer.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 6.
R2 is the owner of the tractor.
R3 is the insurer of R2.
R4 is the owner of the trailer.

R5 is the insurer of R4.
7.

On consideration of the case before the tribunal the tribunal has held that both the owners of the tractor and trailer are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation at the rate of 50% each.
8. However, taking into consideration that the trailer was registered in the Andhra Pradesh and the same was insured in Tamil Nadu at vellore and hence exonerated the insurance company.
9. Before the tribunal, the injured was examined as P.W.1 and Exs.P1 to P16 were marked.
On behalf of the respondents side, RW1 to RW4 were examined and Exs.R1 to R6 were marked.

10. After going through the evidence of R.W.3 and R.W.4, though the tractor is registered in the state of Andhra Pradesh, as could be seen from Ex.R1 and permit AP 36 W 4713 as could be seen in Ex.R3 and policy of insurance https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis for the trailer bearing Registration No.AP 36 W 4714

, I find that the permit is only with regard to state of Andhra Pradesh, however the trailer met with an accident in the jurisdiction of the Tamil Nadu, outside Andhra Pradesh and hence, there is a violation of policy condition.
However, as against third party claimant, it has to be only the pay and recovery and total exoneration of the insurance company cannot be granted.

11. In this view of the matter, the exoneration of the 5th respondent/insurance company is hereby set aside and held that R5 is directed to pay 50% of the award amount along with proportionate costs and interest and recover the same from the owner of R4.
12.

With this modification, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is partly- allowed only to the extent of pay and recovery as stated supra.
